Title: Diagnosis of test `testCodec98NPE`

Details: The test `testCodec98NPE` reads Base64-encoded data from a byte array (derived from a string `Base64TestData.CODEC_98_NPE`) wrapped in a `ByteArrayInputStream`. This stream is then passed into a `Base64InputStream` instance for decoding. The decoded output bytes are obtained via a helper method `Base64TestData.streamToBytes`, which reads all bytes from the provided `InputStream` into a buffer.

The decoding `Base64InputStream` used in the test is constructed with the constructor `Base64InputStream(InputStream)` which delegates to `Base64InputStream(InputStream, boolean)` with `doEncode` set to `false`. This means the stream is in decoding mode, using an internal `Base64` object configured with default settings (`new Base64(false)`).

The helper method `streamToBytes(InputStream, byte[])` reads bytes into the provided buffer by repeatedly calling another helper method `fill(byte[], int, InputStream)`. The `fill` method reads data into the buffer starting at `offset`, updating the read length until the buffer is full or stream ends.

The test fails with a NullPointerException (NPE) on the line calling `streamToBytes`. This suggests that during the reading of the `Base64InputStream`, some unexpected null object is accessed internally.

Given the code signatures and lack of further error trace, the NPE is likely due to an internal null or uninitialized field used during decoding in `Base64InputStream`, probably related to the `Base64` object or buffer management in the decoding mode.

The test data `Base64TestData.CODEC_98_NPE` potentially contains specific input that triggers this corner-case NPE, which was reported to exist in commons-codec version 1.4.

Because the `Base64InputStream` constructor chain and setup appear correct, the fault likely lies in the `Base64InputStream` implementation details for decoding streams—possibly missing initialization or handling of a null buffer, line separator, or decode logic under certain input conditions.

The fault location candidates are in the constructors of `Base64InputStream` and its internal `Base64` decode handling.

Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64InputStream.Base64InputStream(java.io.InputStream)
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64InputStream.Base64InputStream(java.io.InputStream, boolean)
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64InputStream.Base64InputStream(java.io.InputStream, boolean, int, byte[])
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64InputStream.read() (not retrieved but would be relevant)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug.
